items.description: The `Charts` repo carries the library chart source: the shared `_helpers.tpl` content plus the hook Job named template, per design.md.

The library chart is consumable as a single `Chart.yaml` `dependencies:` entry: a consumer chart renders both the shared helpers and the hook Job from that one line, with the named templates carrying the `homelab-shared.*` prefix.

The hook Job the library chart renders matches design.md's skeleton — PreSync hook annotations, `BeforeHookCreation` delete policy, `backoffLimit: 0`, `activeDeadlineSeconds`, the `tf-presync` ServiceAccount, and `hook.repo`/`hook.revision`/`hook.stage` supplied by the consuming app.

items.area: Charts repo — library chart source (R1, ruling)
items.description: HelmCharts' `charts/shared/_helpers.tpl` and every chart's symlink to it are unchanged — un-migrated charts keep consuming it exactly as today, and the two trees diverge deliberately.
The publishing pipeline packages the library chart, regenerates `index.yaml`, and builds the NGINX image carrying both — served at the repository root over plain HTTP inside the pod.
The `index.yaml` entry URLs are absolute under `https://charts.home`, so a client that adds the repository can fetch the tarballs it names.

Publishing a new library version leaves previously published versions resolvable — a chart pinned to an earlier version still renders after a later version publishes — and the mechanism works on the first build, when nothing has been published yet.

The build pushes `registry:5000/charts-home` under both a build-number tag and `:latest`, so HelmCharts resolves it to a live digest at deploy time and a republished image reaches charts.home without a HelmCharts commit.

charts.home is deployed as an ordinary HelmCharts release through the existing harness — a `configs/prd/` release directory the existing pipeline discovers and deploys, with no new pipeline machinery and no storage.
The release lands in namespace `charts-prd`, created by its own `_shared/infrastructure.tf` namespace module — matching the short DNS name `charts`.
The chart-repo image exists in `registry:5000` before the HelmCharts release deploys — otherwise the release is silently absent from the pipeline's stage list rather than failing visibly.
`https://charts.home` resolves and serves over TLS from the homelab CA, same pattern as the estate's other internal endpoints — Service annotations only, no DNS file edit and no Ansible change.
Both the fully-qualified and short names answer, and the certificate is issued for the longest server name with the others as SANs — the estate's `<name>.home, <name>` convention.

A Helm client can add `https://charts.home` as a chart repository and resolve the published library chart version from it. (Proving Argo's repo-server does the same with homelab-CA trust is slice 009's A.5 item, not this one.)

The charts.home chart itself is library-free: it takes no dependency on `homelab-shared` and renders nothing sourced from what charts.home serves, so what deploys charts.home cannot depend on charts.home being up.
The default `registry:5000/argocd-hook:<n>` tag pin lives in the library chart's values — one bump point for the whole estate — and an app can override it while debugging.
`Charts` has its own `.kubecoder/project.yaml` and its curated gate is green from the repo root, so the `../Charts` phases after the first are deterministically gated.

The first deploy of the new namespace, and the Terraform apply behind it, happened on the operator's keystroke: no agent pushed HelmCharts, and the run handed back the exact command and what it would do.
